name: nanoGPT-shakespeare-char
notes: Ran as published — zero patches. Two commands, three real dependencies, 10.65M parameters, 2.5 minutes on one GPU. Best validation loss 1.4666 against the README's quoted 1.4697; and because train.py pins torch.manual_seed(1337), two independent full runs produced bit-identical evaluation curves at all 21 eval points, so this row is replicated and not merely reproduced. prepare.py's four printed dataset statistics matched the expected values recorded in its own source exactly. The only deviations are two flags upstream already defines: --compile=False (drops a host-specific compile warm-up with no payoff at this scale) and --wandb_log=True (turns on the repo's own metric logging, which this config ships off). Findings are all documentation-level: the README's install line omits requests — needed by the very first quick-start command — while listing four packages this recipe never imports; the corpus is fetched from an unpinned master-branch URL; and prepare.py writes its generated data into the source tree with no way to redirect it, so the data directory is an output directory and must be treated as one or the prepare-to-train chain is lost. The one change worth making upstream is small: write the eval history to CSV/JSONL in out_dir unconditionally, so every reproducer gets a durable learning curve without needing a tracking account.
